tasks.title: Your first async function
tasks.statement:
Write async fn greet(name: &str) -> String that returns "Hello, <name>!", and call it with .await in a main with the #[tokio::main] attribute. Print the result for "Anya".

Expected output:
`Hello, Anya!`
tasks.hint: async fn returns a Future; .await inside an async main.

tasks.title: A Future is lazy
tasks.statement:
Create a future f = work() (async fn work prints "work"), print "before", then .await, then print "after". Expected: "before", "work", "after": calling an async fn prints nothing by itself.

Expected output:
`before`
`work`
`after`
tasks.hint: The body runs only on .await.

tasks.title: Order of execution
tasks.statement:
Two async fns a() and b() print "a" and "b". Call them one after another with .await: a, then b, then print "end".

Expected output:
`a`
`b`
`end`
tasks.hint: Sequential .await calls run one after another.

tasks.title: Values from async
tasks.statement:
async fn square(x: u64) -> u64 and async fn sum_squares(n: u64) -> u64, which in a loop calls square(i).await for i from 1 to n. Print sum_squares(10) = 385.

Expected output:
`385`
tasks.hint: Inside an async fn you can call other async fns with .await.

tasks.title: ? in async
tasks.statement:
async fn parse_sum(a: &str, b: &str) -> Result<i32, std::num::ParseIntError>: parse both numbers and add them, using ?. Print the results for («2», «40») and («2», «x») — «Ok(42)» and the error flag «true».

Expected output:
`Ok(42)`
`true`
tasks.hint: ? works in an async fn that returns a Result.

tasks.title: Concurrently: join!
tasks.statement:
Two tasks: the "slow" one sleeps 60 ms and prints "slow", the "fast" one sleeps 10 ms and prints "fast". Run both at once with tokio::join! and print "done" afterwards. Expected: "fast", "slow", "done".

Expected output:
`fast`
`slow`
`done`
tasks.hint: join! runs the futures together; the output order is set by the sleep times.

tasks.title: join! and results
tasks.statement:
async fn fetch(id: u32, ms: u64) -> String: waits ms milliseconds and returns "data <id>". Run fetch(1, 30), fetch(2, 10), fetch(3, 20) through join! and print the results in argument order (not completion order): "data 1 / data 2 / data 3".

Expected output:
`data 1`
`data 2`
`data 3`
tasks.hint: join! returns a tuple of results in argument order.

tasks.title: gather for a list
tasks.statement:
Python: await asyncio.gather(*[f(i) for i in range(5)]). Run 5 identical tasks double(i) (async, sleeps (5 − i)·5 ms and returns 2i) with futures::future::join_all and print the vector of results: [0, 2, 4, 6, 8].

Expected output:
`[0, 2, 4, 6, 8]`
tasks.hint: join_all preserves the order of the input futures.

tasks.title: try_join! stops at an error
tasks.statement:
Two async fns: ok_task() -> Result<u32, String> (returns Ok(1) after 10 ms) and bad_task() -> Result<u32, String> (Err("failure") after 20 ms). Run them with tokio::try_join! and print the result: `Err("failure")`.

Expected output:
`Err("failure")`
tasks.hint: try_join! returns Err at the first error.

tasks.title: spawn instead of create_task
tasks.statement:
Use tokio::spawn to launch a task that sleeps 20 ms and returns 42. Meanwhile main prints "waiting"; then get the result with .await on the handle (it is a Result): "waiting", "42".

Expected output:
`waiting`
`42`
tasks.hint: JoinHandle<T>.await returns Result<T, JoinError>.

tasks.title: Many tasks
tasks.statement:
Launch 100 tasks with spawn; task i returns i·i. Collect the handles in a vector, wait for all of them in order, and print the sum of the results, 328350.

Expected output:
`328350`
tasks.hint: async move carries i into the task.

tasks.title: wait_for → timeout
tasks.statement:
Python: asyncio.wait_for(f(), 0.05). Run a task that sleeps 200 ms under tokio::time::timeout of 50 ms and print "timeout"; then a quick one (10 ms) with the same limit: "success".

Expected output:
`timeout`
`success`
tasks.hint: timeout returns Err(Elapsed) if time ran out.

tasks.title: Who is first
tasks.statement:
Two tasks sleep 30 and 70 ms. Use tokio::select! to print the name of the one that finishes first: "fast".

Expected output:
`fast`
tasks.hint: select! picks the first ready branch and cancels the others.

tasks.title: spawn_blocking
tasks.statement:
Python: run_in_executor. In spawn_blocking compute the sum of the primes below 20000 (a prime has no divisors up to √n) and print it: 21171191.

Expected output:
`21171191`
tasks.hint: spawn_blocking returns a JoinHandle; the computation goes in the closure.

tasks.title: A bridge from plain code
tasks.statement:
In an ordinary fn main (without #[tokio::main]) create a runtime with tokio::runtime::Runtime::new() and run rt.block_on(async { … }), in which you wait 10 ms and return "from async". Print the result.

Expected output:
`from async`
tasks.hint: Runtime::new().unwrap().block_on(…).

tasks.title: block_on from futures
tasks.statement:
Run an async block without tokio: futures::executor::block_on. The block adds the results of the async functions add(2, 3) and add(10, 20) and returns 35. Print the result.

Expected output:
`35`
tasks.hint: block_on runs any future on the current thread.

tasks.title: Different futures in one vector
tasks.statement:
Build a vector of three futures of different types (async blocks that return 1, 2 and 3 after different pauses) as Vec<Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = i32>>>> and run join_all: [1, 2, 3].

Expected output:
`[1, 2, 3]`
tasks.hint: Box::pin(async { … }) gives a Pin<Box<dyn Future>>.

tasks.title: A recursive async function
tasks.statement:
Write a recursive async function fact(n: u64) -> u64 (via Box::pin(fact(n − 1)).await) and print fact(10) = 3628800.

Expected output:
`3628800`
tasks.hint: A recursive async fn must be wrapped in Box::pin: otherwise the state machine would have infinite size.

tasks.title: A stream of values
tasks.statement:
Python: async for. From futures::stream::iter(1..=5) through StreamExt: .map(|x| x * x).filter(|x| ready(x % 2 == 1)).collect::<Vec<_>>().await — print [1, 9, 25].

Expected output:
`[1, 9, 25]`
tasks.hint: StreamExt::filter takes a closure that returns a future: ready(bool).

tasks.title: Completion order
tasks.statement:
Python: asyncio.as_completed. Put three tasks in a FuturesUnordered that sleep 30, 10 and 20 ms and return their own time, and print the results in completion order: 10, 20, 30.

Expected output:
`10`
`20`
`30`
tasks.hint: FuturesUnordered yields results as they become ready.

tasks.title: TaskGroup → JoinSet
tasks.statement:
Start five tasks in a JoinSet; task i sleeps (5 − i)·4 ms and returns i. Collect the results into a vector as they finish and print it sorted: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4], and also the completion order: [4, 3, 2, 1, 0].

Expected output:
`[3, 4, 2, 1, 0]`
`[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`
tasks.hint: set.join_next().await returns Option<Result<T, JoinError>>.

tasks.title: A panic in a task
tasks.statement:
With spawn, launch a task that panics (panic!("boom")) and a second one that returns 7. Print whether the first one has an error (JoinError, is_panic): "true", and the value of the second: "7". The panic message on stderr is not checked.

Expected output:
`true`
`7`
tasks.hint: A panic is isolated in the task and arrives as a JoinError.

tasks.title: Cancelling a task
tasks.statement:
Launch a task that loops forever, sleeping 5 ms and incrementing a shared AtomicUsize. In main wait until the counter is at least 2 (poll with a 5 ms sleep), cancel the task with abort(), and print: "cancelled", then the is_cancelled of the await error: "true".

Expected output:
`cancelled`
`true`
tasks.hint: abort() interrupts the task at the nearest .await.

tasks.title: Send and spawn
tasks.statement:
Write a function run<F>(f: F) -> impl Future<Output = u32>, where F: Future<Output = u32> + Send + 'static, which launches f with tokio::spawn and waits for the result (unwrap). Pass async { 5 + 6 } and print 11.

Expected output:
`11`
tasks.hint: spawn requires Send + 'static.

tasks.title: async move and ownership
tasks.statement:
Create a String s = "planet", move it into an async move block that returns s.len(), run it and print 6. After the block s is unavailable (do not use it).

Expected output:
`6`
tasks.hint: async move takes ownership of the captured values.

tasks.title: Yielding control
tasks.statement:
On a single-threaded runtime (#[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]) launch a task that loops "while the done flag is not set — yield_now().await", counts iterations and then prints "task finished". Main lets it work with one yield_now, raises the flag (AtomicBool), waits for the task and prints "iterations>=1: true".

Expected output:
`task finished`
`iterations>=1: true`
tasks.hint: On a single thread the task cannot advance until main yields control.

tasks.title: Periodic events
tasks.statement:
Python: while True: await asyncio.sleep(…). Create tokio::time::interval(20 ms) and wait for four ticks, measuring the total time: print "4 ticks" and "time >= 60 ms: true" (the first tick fires immediately).

Expected output:
`4 ticks`
`time >= 60 ms: true`
tasks.hint: The first tick() fires immediately, the rest after the period.

tasks.title: A queue between tasks
tasks.statement:
Python: asyncio.Queue. Create tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(8); a producer task sends the numbers 1…5 and finishes; main receives with rx.recv().await until the channel closes and prints the sum, 15.

Expected output:
`15`
tasks.hint: recv returns None when all the senders are dropped.

tasks.title: Shared state
tasks.statement:
Launch 10 tasks, each adding 1 to a shared counter Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<u32>> 100 times. Print the total, 1000.

Expected output:
`1000`
tasks.hint: Clone the Arc into each task; lock().await returns a guard.

tasks.title: One reply
tasks.statement:
Create a oneshot channel; a task sends "answer" after 10 ms; main waits on rx.await and prints "received: answer".

Expected output:
`received: answer`
tasks.hint: oneshot::channel(): one sender, one receiver, one value.
